18.0.s.en: (1) The drought and the search for Elijah

18.0.0.en: The drought continued three years until the word of the Lord came to Elijah, charging him to appear to Ahab, who had kept searching for Elijah while he was hidden throughout those years, and God promised him that He would end the period of drought and give rain. God commanded Elijah to meet Ahab, because Ahab was the king and responsible for all the people, and through him the prophets of Baal and all the people could be summoned, as will appear in the rest of this chapter. For despite the drought that had occurred, Ahab did not return to himself and repent, so the Lord's call came to Elijah to appear, in order to offer Ahab another opportunity for repentance in the story of the priests of Baal, as will come.

18.0.1.en: The New Testament mentions in (Lk 4:25, Jas 5:17) that the duration of the drought was three years and six months, while here it says three years. The difference is that Elijah's first meeting with Ahab was in the spring season, in which no rain falls until the beginning of the next month, about six months, which the New Testament included, while here the duration is counted from the beginning of the winter following the spring.

18.0.2.en: God had withheld the rain because of the people's departure from the worship of God and their worship of Baal under the leadership of Jezebel and Ahab, who also killed the prophets of God. Despite the hardness of the hearts of Ahab and Jezebel, the people were affected by the famine and began to return to God, or became ready to repent and reject the worship of idols; therefore God told Elijah that He would send rain. This shows that God permits affliction to draw His people to repentance, but He is full of tenderness, so that when they begin to respond He overflows upon them with His blessings.

18.1.0.en: Elijah carried out the divine command at once and went to meet Ahab in Samaria. There he noticed the suffering of the people because of the famine.

18.2.0.en: Ahab had appointed Obadiah as steward of the affairs of his palace, and he trusted him and entrusted his palace to him. This Obadiah was a godly man who feared the Lord. Thus we find that the wicked Ahab entrusted his house to no one but a godly man who worshiped God, because the godly are the faithful ones in whom all trust, even the wicked.

18.2.1.en: Hold fast to the commandments of God, and you will please Him and obtain His blessing, and He will give you favor in the eyes of all, and you will even be a preacher of God among the wicked, to bring them back to God.

18.3.1.en: When Jezebel was hunting the prophets of the Lord to destroy them, Obadiah worked to rescue them from her hand by taking 100 prophets from the school of the prophets and placing fifty of them in each cave, and he used to bring them bread and water to keep them alive in the time of the drought, that is, he fed them throughout the famine, and from this we conclude the following:

18.3.2.en: 1- The persecution by Ahab and Jezebel of the prophets of God and the killing of many of them, since she felt the weakness of her gods to bring down rain, so she ascribed the drought to the men of God and tried to kill them, especially since Elijah had escaped from her hand into the wildernesses.

18.3.3.en: 2- The courage of Obadiah, his faith and his generosity in caring to provide for 100 prophets from the school of the prophets, and so we find mention of the school of the prophets after the age of Ahab, as in (2 Kgs 2:1, 2, 4).

18.3.4.en: 3- The prophets of God were in isolation from the people, living a life of solitude to pray for the people. It is understood from this that Jezebel was not able to cut off all the prophets of God, as is proved by:

18.3.5.en: 1- Obadiah was able to hide a hundred prophets of God.

18.3.6.en: 2- The existence of schools of the prophets in the days of Elisha, as we mentioned.

18.3.7.en: 3- The existence of seven thousand knees that had not bowed to Baal, as God told Elijah (ch. 19:18), and there may be among them a number of prophets of God.

18.3.8.en: And because Jezebel encouraged the worship of idols, she did not kill the prophets who served the golden calves that Jeroboam had set up in Bethel and Dan, nor did she kill those who offered sacrifices to the idols on the high places in Israel; four hundred of these prophets are mentioned in (ch. 22:6).

18.4.0.en: What occupied Ahab's mind in the time of the drought was not the life of his people but the life of his animals, horses and mules. Here he asks Obadiah, who was in charge of them, to go out with him to search for springs of water or valleys, so as to keep alive as many of his beasts as he could. He certainly imported food from the surrounding countries, such as Egypt, for himself and those with him, and left his people to die of hunger. And despite all that the drought did in the land, Ahab and Jezebel did not repent and return to God, confessing their sins, which were the cause of the drought.

18.5.0.en: He decided that each of them should go in a different direction from the other, so that they could search for water over the largest possible area of the land, and this shows that the drought was severe and the rivers had dried up, so they tried to search for any springs in which there was still water.

18.6.0.en: While Obadiah was carrying out the mission that the king had given him, he met Elijah face to face and bowed down before him, and although he knew him personally he asked Elijah to confirm that it was he. Of course Elijah's meeting with Obadiah was by God's arrangement, and Obadiah was astonished at Elijah's appearance, since Ahab was searching for him to kill him, but he certainly rejoiced in the blessing of the meeting, because Elijah represented the voice of God in the wicked kingdom that had departed from God and attached itself to the worship of idols.

18.7.0.en: Elijah assured him that it was he, and charged him to go back to his lord Ahab and tell him that he had found him.

18.8.0.en: Obadiah told Elijah that this message which Elijah had given him to carry exposed him to the danger of death, for the following reasons:

18.8.1.en: 1- Because Ahab would be angry with him for not seizing Elijah, and might kill him.

18.8.2.en: 2- Ahab had sent and searched for Elijah in every place in the kingdom and the surrounding kingdoms and made them swear, that is, charged them strictly, to seize Elijah so that he might come and pray and lift the drought, and all were unable to find Elijah.

18.8.3.en: 3- If he told Ahab that he had found Elijah, and asked him to come with him to meet him at the appointed place, and after he had brought him he might not find Elijah, for the Spirit of God would carry him, as was customary, to some other place, then Ahab would feel that Obadiah was mocking him and would order him killed. Obadiah believed that God protects His prophet Elijah from the hand of Ahab, who wanted to kill him, and carries him to any place and hides him there, as He had rescued him throughout the previous three and a half years and rescued him from the hand of Ahab.

18.8.4.en: In the end Obadiah begged Elijah not to let him die, because he feared God and did not worship Baal as Ahab and the rest of the people did.

18.9.0.en: Obadiah mentioned to Elijah that he had cared to provide for a hundred of the sons of the prophets, so that this might intercede for him and Elijah would not expose him to the danger of death by making him carry this message to Ahab. Obadiah was one of the best of the godly who lived in the days of Ahab, who worshiped God and did not worship Baal, but secretly, lest Ahab kill them; he also cared for the prophets of God, but also secretly. He did not have the strength of Elijah to proclaim the truth even if he were exposed to death, but this does not cancel his piety and his love for God.

18.10.0.en: Elijah, who felt the presence of God at every moment, which he had become accustomed to in his seclusion in the wilderness, pledged and assured Obadiah that he would meet Ahab on this very day, that he might be reassured. Elijah mentioned the Lord of hosts as a title of God in order to assure Obadiah of two things:

18.10.1.en: 1- That he pledges before the mighty God who is able to do all things, so his pledge is sure.

18.10.2.en: 2- To reassure Obadiah, so that he would not fear the power of Ahab, since it is nothing before the power of God.

18.11.0.en: Then Obadiah was reassured, confident of Elijah's truthfulness, so he went back to where he found Ahab and told him that he had found Elijah, and Ahab went to meet Elijah, and this of course was more important than finding springs of water and grass. Here appears the weakness of Ahab before the power of God that was in Elijah, for the king went to Elijah, in whose hand was the life of all the people and of Ahab himself. For God gives His children awe and a power that subdues the wicked to them.

18.12.0.en: When Ahab reached Elijah, the evil of Ahab appeared, who had not repented until now of his sins despite the severity of the drought, so he accused Elijah of being the cause of the severe affliction that had come upon the kingdom of Israel, by his withholding the rain, so that this great famine occurred. Perhaps by this he wanted to stir up the people who were with him against Elijah.

18.13.0.en: Baalim: the plural of Baal, since the name of Baal was applied to many cities and places, so Elijah means every Baal they worship; the introduction of the worship of Baal into Israel was at the hand of Ahab and Jezebel his wife. With all strength and courage the prophet denied the accusation directed at him, and with all boldness the prophet turned the accusation back upon the king and the house of his father, showing him that the cause of the wrath that had come upon the land, by the withholding of water, was the neglect of the commandments of the Lord and the worship of idols, in which Ahab and all his house had walked.

18.13.1.en: And whoever troubles the people of God deserves stoning and death, as happened with Achan the son of Carmi in the days of Joshua (Josh 7:25). Elijah's saying to Ahab "in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord" means all the people, whom Ahab leads, but he also said to Ahab "thou hast followed Baalim," that is, in the singular, because the one who introduced the worship of the Baalim into Israel was Ahab.

18.14.s.en: (2) The acceptance of Elijah's sacrifice and the killing of the prophets of Baal

18.14.0.en: Mount Carmel: a mountain extending from the east of Palestine to near the Mediterranean Sea, a distance of about thirteen miles, and the river Kishon extends south of the mountain from the east and heads northwest until it flows into the Mediterranean Sea at a place south of the city of Haifa. At the top of its summit is an area called the Burnt Offering (al-Muhraqa), where Elijah offered his sacrifice; it is a huge flat area on the mountain with an elevation of about one thousand seven hundred feet above sea level, and it lies in its eastern part.

18.14.1.en: The prophets of Baal: they claimed to be prophets while they were liars, so they were called prophets, and Baal is the sun-god, whom Ahab worshiped.

18.14.2.en: The prophets of the groves: groves were set up, that is, wooden pillars, for the worship of the goddess Ashtoreth, who is the moon-goddess, whom Jezebel worshiped.

18.14.3.en: Which eat at Jezebel's table: Jezebel fed them and cared for their needs.

18.14.4.en: Ahab was in great need of the falling of rain because of the intensity of the hunger, so when Elijah spoke to him with authority and commanded him to gather all Israel, that is, the heads of all the people, and also to bring the prophets of Baal, who numbered four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves, whom Jezebel cared for, who numbered four hundred, Ahab obeyed in submission and carried out the command quickly, and he was like a child before a great master, because the power of God was in Elijah. Perhaps he was reassured that the number of his prophets was very large and Elijah was one person, so he did not fear the confrontation, and perhaps he thought that Elijah wanted to show his authority by bringing down rain before all the heads and officials of the kingdom and did not imagine anything else.

18.14.5.en: Elijah chose Mount Carmel and the place that he specified, which was afterward called the Burnt Offering, for the following reasons:

18.14.6.en: 1- There was in this place an old altar that Elijah repaired (v. 30), and perhaps it was from the days of the patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, so it was a holy place in the eyes of the people.

18.14.7.en: 2- Because of the height of the mountain, the fire upon it can be seen from a great distance, so Jezebel and very many of the people would see it.

18.14.8.en: 3- The mountain is in a central place between the dwelling places of the tribes, so the largest number of the people could see what happened on it.

18.14.9.en: 4- Because of the height of the mountain, one can also see from it the sky and the clouds, which foretell the coming of rain.

18.14.10.en: 5- The Canaanites considered this mountain a dwelling of their gods, so it was an opportunity for Elijah to proclaim the power of God, which is above all gods, because of the sanctity of this place, especially after what Elijah did on it; it became a holy place in the eyes of the people, and so the prophet Elisha made a dwelling for himself on it (2 Kgs 4:25). It appears that Jezebel was more fearful than Ahab, so she prevented the prophets of the groves from going to this confrontation, to which none went but the prophets of Baal (v. 22); perhaps she feared to show the weakness of her gods before the power of God, or that any harm would befall her prophets.

18.15.0.en: Before the power of the word of God on the mouth of Elijah the king obeyed at once and sent and gathered the heads of the people, that is, the heads of the tribes and clans, and all the prophets of Baal, because the king was in great weakness through the intensity of the famine, and he thought that Elijah was commanding the gathering of all these to show his authority in bringing down rain.

18.16.0.en: Halt between two opinions: the lame person, because of the weakness of his legs, leans to the right and then to the left and cannot walk straight with steady steps.

18.16.1.en: The people were surprised that Elijah did not pray for the rain to come down, but confronted them with the cause of the problems they were suffering from, that is, the famine, namely their departure from God and their mixing His worship with the worship of idols. They had seen in God the power and authority over all things, as He had done with their fathers from of old, and they saw in the worship of Baal a pleasing of the king and a satisfaction of their evil lusts that accompany pagan worship. And here in Elijah's question he demands that they choose whom they will worship, either God or Baal, because the two kinds of worship cannot be mixed, for this does not please God. Before this plain question the heads of the people were silent, because they realized their error, and perhaps they still wanted to hold to both forms of worship, because they could not leave God, the true God, while at the same time they still feared the king and wanted to satisfy their lusts, and therefore they needed a power to shake them and restore their faith in God, and this is what Elijah would do in the following verses. They found nothing with which to answer Elijah. It is noticed that Elijah did not ask the king or the prophets of Baal, because they were wicked, attached to the worship of idols and rejecting God.

18.16.2.en: God wants all your heart, your soul, your mind and your strength, so let not your heart be occupied with both God and the world, because the love of the world is enmity with God. God also gave you Himself on the cross and gives you His Body and Blood on the altar every day, so the least response is to give Him your life, as He gave you His life; then you will be filled with satisfaction and strength and live in assurance and with good things that cannot be expressed.

18.17.0.en: Elijah continued his speech with the heads of the people and said to them, "I, even I only, remain a prophet of the Lord," who proclaims His name in all the kingdom; for although there were other prophets, such as those whom Obadiah was feeding (v. 13), they were all hidden for fear of the violence of Ahab. He also said that there were now four hundred and fifty pagan prophets who worshiped Baal, so he was one against four hundred and fifty, yet he speaks with faith and authority and does not fear the great number before him, nor their loud voices, nor the king's support of them. It is noticed that the prophets of the groves, who numbered four hundred, whom Jezebel cared for and fed, did not attend this meeting, although Elijah had asked Ahab to summon them; perhaps Jezebel feared for them from the power of Elijah and his God, and this shows that Jezebel and Ahab, despite their evil, feared Elijah, but they did not submit to the fear of God and persisted in the worship of idols.

18.18.0.en: Elijah added and said to the people, so that you may know who is the true God: let them give us two bullocks, and let the prophets of Baal come forward and choose one bullock, and slay it and cut it in pieces and offer it as a sacrifice to their god Baal, and let us see whether he will bring down fire from heaven to consume the sacrifice, or not. And I will offer the other bullock as a sacrifice, and we shall see whether God will bring down fire from heaven to consume it, or not. The people approved this proposal, since Elijah was able to influence their hearts and arouse in them the love of the one God as they had learned from their fathers, and because the power of God was with him, the Spirit of God was able to influence hearts, and they submitted to Elijah's proposal and even approved it, so that the prophets of Baal could not afterward refuse Elijah's challenge to them, and perhaps they were hoping that Baal could bring down fire from heaven, because he had authority over fire, as they claim.

18.18.1.en: It is noticed that Baal is the sun-god, who is known to his followers to have authority over fire and rain, so here Elijah exposes Baal, because when he is unable to bring down fire this shows his weakness before the people, and therefore his inability also to lift the famine by bringing down rain.

18.18.2.en: Elijah's call was strange to the minds of the people, because he asked them to worship either God or Baal, and the fire would come down from heaven from God or Baal to declare the acceptance of the sacrifice; it is not possible to worship the two together, at the time when the worshipers of Baal welcomed the worship of any other god beside their god, such as the goddess Ashtoreth, for whom they had set up the groves. So the idol worshipers seem to be courteous and tolerant and to accept other forms of worship, and Elijah to be the rigid one who has no love, since he wants the worship of God alone; but all this did not weaken Elijah, and he proclaimed his faith and his challenge to the pagan god Baal.

18.18.3.en: Hold fast to your faith, and do not accept ideas foreign to the Church under the pretext of tolerance and love, even if some accuse you of rigidity and of limiting entry into heaven to yourself and those who believe the faith of your Church. Be strong like Elijah and pray for all, but do not give up your faith for which the martyrs died.

18.19.0.en: After Elijah had spoken to the people as above, he directed his words to the prophets of Baal and said to them, begin by offering your bullock as a sacrifice and put no fire under it, and ask your god to bring down fire and accept your sacrifice. He told them to begin because they were greater in number, and this was wisdom on his part, for after they fail to have their sacrifice accepted and no fire comes down, he comes forward and succeeds in bringing down the fire, and it appears that his God is the true God. For if he had begun first and the fire had come down on his sacrifice, they might have said, we too can, and there might have been confusion and their inability would not have appeared; but their beginning to offer the sacrifice and their failure shows clearly the weakness of their god Baal and that what they claim of his authority over fire is a lie. Elijah left to the prophets of Baal to choose the bullock they wanted, lest they say that Elijah had chosen a good bullock and left them a bullock with defects that their gods, that is, the Baalim, the plural of Baal, would reject.

18.19.1.en: It is noticed from all this that Elijah delayed the bringing down of rain in order to treat the cause of the problems, which was the weakness of their faith in God and their worship of idols, so that they might repent and return to God, and then He would give them rain as a divine gift from Him to His obedient children.

18.20.0.en: The prophets of Baal came forward and set up an altar, or repaired an old altar of Baal that was in this place, and offered their sacrifice on it, that is, they cut it up and laid it on it, then raised their prayers to Baal that he would accept their sacrifice, and they continued a long time in prayer, from the morning until noon, and they danced around the altar, because they believed that Baal was pleased with them by dancing, as they also believed in many mistaken practices such as fornication, for they satisfied their lusts, or Satan moved them to that, so that the pagan gods would be pleased with them; but all their prayers and dancing were of no use and no fire came down from heaven, so they were in great embarrassment and distress before the people. Perhaps the prophets of Baal believed that the power of their god, who is the sun-god, appears clearly when its heat intensifies at noon, so they cried out and danced until noon, but nothing happened.

18.20.1.en: We see here that the prophets of Baal and Elijah present the same form of worship, which is a sacrifice, so that the gods may be pleased with them, but there is a vast difference between the worship of God and the worship of idols. Satan was and still is imitating the form of true worship but with foreign ideas, to lead men astray from the true worship of God, and whoever does not examine carefully may think that all forms of worship are one and be deceived and go astray, so he leaves his Church and departs from God. So be careful, do not listen to ideas foreign to your Church, or be drawn to any worship that differs from your Church.

18.21.0.en: After the prayers and dancing of the prophets of Baal for a long time until noon, Elijah said to them, cry aloud to your god, for a god in his greatness may need a loud voice, and by this he mocks them, because God sees and hears everything, even if it is in a low voice. Then he said to them, perhaps your god is absorbed in some particular thought and not attentive to what you say, and of course logically this is wrong, for how could a god not watch over his followers, when he is spirit and not man, so how could he be absorbed in a thought that prevents him from hearing the prayers of his followers? He also said to them, perhaps your god is in seclusion, and this the mind does not accept, because he is not a man who withdraws from people and goes into seclusion, but a spirit who does not need seclusion, so he belittles their god. Elijah also added the possibility that he is on a journey, and of course distances mean nothing to spirits, for they are able to hear from afar. By all this he warns the people that the pagan gods are not gods and have no existence, that perhaps they would take heed and return to God, the true God, in whom there are none of all these weaknesses. Then he said to them finally, perhaps their god is asleep, and of course a spirit does not sleep.

18.22.0.en: It is remarkable that the prophets of Baal believed what Elijah said, who was mocking them, for they thought that their god Baal was in seclusion, or asleep, and so on, and they cried out with loud voices, and in their hands were swords with which they began to cut themselves until their blood gushed out. This was a custom of theirs in their prayers, so that perhaps when their god saw their blood flowing he would take pity on them and answer them. Thus they lived in superstitions that Satan made them imagine.

18.23.0.en: Noon: the sixth hour for the Jews, which corresponds to twelve noon in our time.

18.23.1.en: They prophesied: they prayed and called upon their god and cried out to him.

18.23.2.en: At the offering of the oblation: that is, the ninth hour for the Jews, which corresponds to three in the afternoon, when the evening burnt offering was offered.

18.23.3.en: The prophets of Baal continued crying out from the morning until noon, and then until three in the afternoon, but their god Baal did not answer them with anything and no fire came down from heaven, so they were in great failure and despair. Why did the prophets of Baal fail to bring down fire? And how was Satan unable to bring down fire? And how did Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal to offer a sacrifice to see who could bring down fire, God or Baal? All this goes back to Elijah's faith in the power of God, and the presence of Elijah as a prophet of God proclaims the presence of God, and in the presence of God every satanic work fails; that is, it was impossible for them to bring down fire in the presence of Elijah, because the power of God that was in him stops the work of Satan, as the inability of the magicians appeared in the days of Moses when they turned their rods into serpents and the serpent of Moses' rod swallowed them up (Ex 7:12).

18.24.0.en: When the third hour after noon came, there was no more time for Elijah to wait, because the evening was near, so he came forward and called all the heads of the people to see the work of God and His acceptance of his sacrifice, and he repaired an old altar of God that was probably in this region from the days of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

18.25.0.en: Elijah used in the repair of the altar twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, who is Israel, for despite the division of the kingdom he believes that they are one people and that the tribes must return to be one people, and this is what happened after the captivity.

18.26.0.en: Elijah built an altar in the name of the Lord, that is, it is different from the altar of Baal and all pagan altars, and on it the miracle and the divine revelation would take place.

18.26.1.en: After he built the altar he dug around it a deep trench as great as would contain two measures of seed, and probably what is meant is not the volume of two measures, since a measure equals twelve cups, that is, about eight and a half liters, but that the depth of the trench was the height of a sack or bag holding two measures; in sum, it was a deep trench. He made this trench because in some pagan forms of worship they would dig a trench and put fire in it, and it would come out from under the altar and consume the sacrifice, whereas here he would put water in the trench, that the people might be sure that there was no fire on the ground and around the altar.

18.27.0.en: After Elijah built the altar he arranged the wood upon it in order, because our God is a God of order and so that the power of the miracle might appear, for Elijah hides nothing among the wood, as there could be if it were placed in heaps. Then he laid the bullock on the arranged wood, after he had cut it into pieces, and then commanded his helpers to fill four barrels with water and pour it on the bullock and the wood and the altar, so everything was drenched with water and it ran down from the altar and fell into the trench dug around it. Then he asked them to pour four barrels a second time, and four barrels a third time, until the water covered everything and filled the deep trench surrounding the altar, so that any doubt might be removed that there was a source of fire hidden in the altar and around it, as some pagans used to do. This shows the extent of Elijah's confidence in God, who would bring down a mighty fire from heaven that could devour the sacrifice however soaked with water it was.

18.28.0.en: At the time of the offering of the oblation: the time of the evening burnt offering which the Law commanded to be made, and which was offered daily on behalf of the people before God that He might be pleased with them, and which is a symbol of the sacrifice of Christ on the cross, by which He pleased the Father.

18.28.1.en: After Elijah had arranged and built the altar, the burnt offering and the wood, and put the water on them, he waited until the time came for offering the evening sacrifice, that is, from three o'clock to five in the evening, in order to declare that God rejoices when worship is offered to Him at its appointed times, and reveals Himself to His children at this time and confirms their faith. At this time Elijah stood and prayed to God, and his prayer contained the following:

18.28.2.en: 1- He reminded God of His promises that He gave to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and he substituted the word Israel for Jacob, in whom the prophecies were fulfilled.

18.28.3.en: 2- The proclamation of the power of God, which surpasses all the pagan gods, that the people of God might believe in Him and that He might appear before all the nations.

18.28.4.en: 3- Showing that Elijah is the servant of God who carries out His commands, for it is God who commanded the withholding of the rain and the occurrence of the famine, that the people might repent and believe that He is the only God, especially when He accepts the sacrifice by fire from heaven.

18.29.0.en: Thou hast turned their heart back again: they began to return to God by faith and repentance from the worship of idols.

18.29.1.en: Elijah asked God urgently to answer his prayer, for his faith in God does not cancel importunity, since this shows the extent of his faith and his clinging to God, and he told God that he asked His answer by bringing down the fire to consume the sacrifice for two reasons, which are:

18.29.2.en: 1- To show clearly that God is the only God and all the pagan gods are nothing.

18.29.3.en: 2- If He had stirred the feelings of the people to believe in Him and repent, when Elijah confronted them with the question to choose whether to worship either God or Baal, since it is not possible to combine them (v. 21), and then when the inability of the prophets of Baal to bring down fire to consume their sacrifice appeared, now he asks that the faith and repentance of the people be completed when the fire comes down to consume his sacrifice, and this shows that a man's repentance and faith do not come in a moment but come in steps until they are complete.

18.29.4.en: If you have a petition before God, wait on Him and press Him, and declare to Him that you will not leave Him and that you trust in His ability to solve your problem, for God rejoices in your faith and your importunity.

18.30.0.en: After Elijah's deep, powerful prayer, full of importunity, God showed His glory before all the people and fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifice and the wood under it and the stones under the wood that formed the altar and the dust under the altar, and by the power of the fire it was even able to touch the much water that was around the altar, so the whole place became burned with fire.

18.30.1.en: This fire certainly came down from heaven, as is proved by the following:

18.30.2.en: 1- There was no lightning or rain or the possibility of fire coming down from natural phenomena.

18.30.3.en: 2- The fire consumed the sacrifice, then the wood and after it the stones and below them the dust and the water, that is, it came down from above to below and not like the nature of fire, which rises from below to above.

18.30.4.en: 3- The touching of the fire to the water confirms that there was no fire hidden beneath the altar, as the pagans used to do in their worship.

18.30.5.en: 4- In the case of ordinary fire, it kindles the wood, which burns the sacrifice, but in this case the fire burned the sacrifice before the wood caught fire.

18.30.6.en: The drenching of the sacrifice with water is a symbol of the sacrament of Baptism, in which a man is immersed in water, and the heavenly fire is a symbol of the work of the Holy Spirit in the sacrament, who came down at the prayer of Elijah, who is a symbol of the priest. The burning by fire of the twelve stones, which represent the people of God with its twelve tribes, is a symbol of God's calling His people to offer their lives as a sacrifice of love, that they may enjoy the overflow of His love and mercy.

18.30.7.en: The people were far from God, attached to the worship of idols, and so deserved to be burned by the fire of divine wrath, but only the sacrifice was burned instead of all the people, and it is a symbol of Christ, who died for mankind and redeemed it.

18.30.8.en: God is ready to work powerful miracles if the matter requires, so trust in that; He is able to solve your problems in quiet ways that people do not notice, except you, or by a great work visible to all, but in every case believe in Him and press Him, for He will surely intervene and solve your problem.

18.31.0.en: As a result of this divine miracle of the coming down of fire from heaven, the following occurred:

18.31.1.en: 1- The people declared their submission to God alone by their bowing down before Him and their readiness to obey His commandments and orders.

18.31.2.en: 2- They declared strongly that the Lord is the God alone and repeated that, confirming their faith, and by this God answered the petition of Elijah (v. 37) and supported him and was glorified before all His people.

18.32.0.en: Elijah commanded the people to seize all the prophets of Baal and let none of them escape and to bring them down to the river Kishon, and there he commanded that they be slain, and by this he fulfills two things:

18.32.1.en: 1- Confirming their faith in God, by cutting off the evil from among them and removing it.

18.32.2.en: 2- Their taking part in the purification of the land so as to regain their confidence in themselves as children of God.

18.32.3.en: Elijah's slaying of the prophets of Baal was not cruelty on his part, as is proved by the following:

18.32.4.en: 1- This was the carrying out of the Law of God, which commands the killing of whoever incites another to the worship of idols (Deut 13:6-9).

18.32.5.en: 2- The slaying of the priests was a command from God to Elijah, as appears from (v. 36).

18.32.6.en: 3- Had Elijah been lax and left the prophets of Baal alive, and most of them were probably Jews and not foreigners, they would have worked again to mislead the people and their worship of idols.

18.32.7.en: Thus Elijah removed the prophets of Baal at the river Kishon, which is still called the river of the slaughter, where the heads of these wicked men were cut off.

18.33.1.en: After Elijah killed the prophets of Baal, he looked at King Ahab, who had been fasting because of his agitation over the expected event of Elijah's confrontation with the prophets of Baal and the heads of the people, and he had been watching what those prophets did in their prayers and their cutting of themselves with swords, and then the coming down of the fire to consume Elijah's sacrifice. Perhaps he wanted to know the truth, who is the greater God, the God of Elijah or Baal? All this made him unwilling to eat; and after the king saw the killing of his prophets he was not troubled, because he began to feel with the rest of the people that God is the true God; therefore Elijah said to him: go up from the river Kishon to the high place on Mount Carmel where tents had been set up for the king and a table for him to eat, because the time had passed four or five in the afternoon.

18.33.2.en: Elijah told Ahab that he heard the sound of an abundance of rain, though it was not a sound heard by the ears of Ahab and all who stood by, but Elijah heard it by the spirit of prophecy.

18.33.3.en: Probably at this time the heads of the people began to depart after this long day with its powerful events, and Elijah is blamed for not making use of the opportunity of the gathering of the heads of the people from all regions of the kingdom, their being moved by what had happened and their declaring their faith in God, to lead them in specific steps to begin the new life with God, such as returning to God by daily prayer, holding fast to His commandments and His Law and getting rid of the statues of Baal set up in their various lands. This is the natural completion that he should have done, because he knows that men are moved and then forget what they felt and return to their former wicked life after a period. His being occupied with bringing down the rain, which was the people's first demand, if he had delayed an hour to preach to the people, would have been better; but Elijah, despite his greatness, was also a man with his weaknesses.

18.33.4.en: On the other hand, we see God's response to the need of His people, for after they declared their faith in Him God intervened by His power to lift the famine, and He announced to Elijah that the rain would come down in power, and he in turn announced it to the king and all who stood around him.

18.34.0.en: The king obeyed the word of Elijah, since he was convinced of the power of God and of His prophet Elijah, and he did not care about the death of his prophets, because he knew that they were deceivers, in addition to his need for food, so he went up to where a table had been prepared for him on the high place near the place where Elijah's sacrifice was accepted.

18.34.1.en: Elijah, however, went up from the river Kishon to a high place on Mount Carmel from which he could see the sea, and only his servant followed him. There on the top of the mountain Elijah bowed down on the earth and began to pray that God would have compassion on His people and send the rain and lift the famine, and probably his prayers first included thanksgiving to God, because He had intervened and revealed Himself through the fire coming down from heaven, and by this He supported His prophet Elijah before all the people and brought them back to His worship. So words of thanksgiving mingled with supplication to God to complete His work and have mercy on His people and give them rain. This bowing down and the prayers accompanying it confirm Elijah's humility and faith in God, who is able to do all things, and also his lowliness, for in his prostration he put his head to the ground with his face between his knees, and so he proclaims his weakness and his need of God.

18.34.2.en: Although God had called Elijah to meet Ahab and tell him that the rain would come (v. 1), he prayed much for the rain to come down. The promises of God do not make us slack in prayer, fasting and every act of worship; on the contrary, they draw us to increase them, so that we may enjoy the fulfillment of these promises and our love and attachment to God may increase, for the promises have no effect if we do not pray and press God to bestow them on us.

18.34.3.en: We also see that Elijah was not occupied with his glory after the coming down of the fire, for he did not stand to receive the praise of the people, but hurried to complete his work of solving the problem by bringing down the rain.

18.35.0.en: After Elijah prayed, he sent his servant to a higher place on the mountain, to see the sea clearly from there, where the clouds begin to appear from afar, then move until they come to the middle of the sky, and after that the rains come down. The servant went and saw nothing, so he returned and told Elijah so.

18.35.1.en: Elijah continued his prayers with more lowliness and supplication before God, then returned and sent his servant to look at the sea from afar, but he found nothing and returned and told Elijah so. Elijah continued in his prayers and in sending his servant, so that he sent him seven times. These prayers show Elijah's faith and his importunity at the same time and his supplication for the sake of all the people; the heads of the people should have continued with him in prayer, but they departed because of their weakness, while he, as a representative of them, continued to pray.

18.35.2.en: God did not send the rain quickly in order to show the greatness of Elijah's faith, his humility and his clinging to prayer, so that he might be an example for this people, that they might return to God and hold fast to prayer.

18.35.3.en: When you see some sins and weaknesses in those around you, do not judge them, but ask God for them, and according to their need offer prayers, fasts and prostrations (metanoias); by this you will be a true servant and one who loves those around you.

18.36.0.en: The seventh time, Elijah's servant saw a little cloud, which he saw with difficulty because it was like the size of a man's hand, rising out of the sea, that is, from the farthest part of the sky, so he rejoiced and hurried to tell Elijah that there was hope of clouds appearing and rain coming down. Elijah, however, understood that this little cloud was the beginning of very many clouds that would cover the sky and bring down heavy rains; therefore he commanded his servant to hurry to the king, who was on the high place above Mount Carmel, and tell him to hurry to go to his palace in Jezreel, so that the heavy rain would not hinder him from that. From this we understand that we should not despise any divine blessing, even if it appears small, because it may be the beginning of abundant blessings; as the Incarnation of Christ as a little child in a manger was the beginning of the redemption of mankind on the cross, which all generations awaited.

18.37.0.en: Quickly the clouds filled the sky and a stormy wind blew and heavy rain poured down, and Ahab hurried in his chariot toward Jezreel, where Ahab had a palace other than his palace in Samaria, the capital of his kingdom.

18.38.0.en: Elijah was from a city like those in the mountain of Gilead east of the river Jordan, and the inhabitants of this mountainous region were distinguished by tall stature and physical strength, in addition to the fact that Elijah lived in the wildernesses most of his life, so his ability to walk and run was great; but it is unreasonable that he should outrun the chariot of King Ahab, drawn by horses, from Mount Carmel to Jezreel, where the king had a palace in which he spent the winter season, in addition to his great palace in his capital Samaria. The distance from Carmel to Jezreel was about fifteen miles, but the verse here mentions that the hand of the Lord was on Elijah, so it is understood from this that the Spirit of God carried him part of this distance, but he was running, perhaps at the beginning of the way, before the king's chariot, and then after this he reached Jezreel before the royal chariot. In this running we sense two things:

18.38.1.en: 1- Support for King Ahab, for he ran before him, that is, he was one of his followers accompanying him, and this encourages him to stand firm in faith in God and rejection of Baal and repentance from pagan worship, so that he would not waver when he met the wicked Jezebel, the pagan, attached to idols and strong in personality, who used to influence him. Perhaps when he saw Elijah running quickly, then the Spirit of God carrying him, then his outrunning him to Jezreel, he would be certain of the power of God that was in him and hold fast to the faith that Elijah proclaimed.

18.38.2.en: 2- To be in Jezreel to receive the message of the wicked Jezebel, which she would send to him, as we shall see. From what has gone before we see Elijah's activity and his use of time: he had assembled from the morning with the king and the prophets of Baal and the heads of the people, and waited until noon for the prophets of Baal to pray, then repaired the altar, prepared his sacrifice and offered it at three in the afternoon, and after that God accepted it by fire from heaven and the people declared their faith in Him, then he seized the prophets of Baal and led them to the river Kishon and slew them there, and this took time until four-thirty; then he spent about an hour in prayer until the rain came down, and after that he ran before the chariot until he reached Jezreel, and this took half an hour or more, so that he reached Jezreel at the end of the day. This is an example of the true servant, who works always, and God supports him with power.

18.38.3.en: God appears to Elijah the fugitive
